title: Add hardware-split token metrics and synthetic replaybench for cost attribution
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Introduces per-token hardware attribution metrics (CPU vs GPU) and a synthetic replaybench to estimate production cost split. Backwards-compatible metrics added behind a runtime flag; dashboards and alert tuning included.
description:
Motivation: Customers frequently ask why some invocations are expensive even when model latency is OK. We previously had only token-level aggregate cost estimates that lumped CPU and GPU together. This PR adds explicit per-token hardware attribution (CPU vs GPU execution time and token-level I/O overhead) and a synthetic replaybench that replays sampled traces with hardware routing flags to estimate cost splits across deployments.

What this change does:
- Adds new metrics exported by runtime workers: invocation_token_cpu_ms_total, invocation_token_gpu_ms_total, invocation_token_io_ms_total, token_hardware_fraction{hw="cpu"|"gpu"}. Metrics are aggregated per-invocation and exposed with per-tenant labels.
- Introduces a lightweight sampling/opt-in hook (runtime config flag runtime.metrics.hw_split_enabled) so customers can enable measurements without global perf impact.
- Implements a synthetic replaybench service (observability/replaybench) that consumes sampled invocation traces, replays them against the runtime with controlled hardware routing and collects hardware-split metrics to build cost attribution profiles. The replaybench accepts a date range and sampling seed for reproducible runs.
- Adds Grafana dashboard panels and a small explorer to visualize per-route and per-model hardware split, token-rate stacked bars, and an alert panel that triggers when token_hardware_fraction{hw="cpu"} rises above a configured threshold for a route.
- Adjusts alerting: new alert rule (SRE-HW-SPLIT-01) uses a 60m rolling window and de-duplicates noisy spikes by looking at replaybench-confirmed regressions.
- Documentation: runtime flag, SDK tagging (invocation.metadata.hw_hint), and a short howto for running the replaybench locally.

Design notes and tradeoffs:
- We measure CPU time using a per-worker lightweight timer (no sampling of syscalls) and correlate with GPU timestamps from the batch execution path. Because GPU timestamps are coarse across batches, we add a per-token attribution heuristic: GPU time is divided by token emission count in the batch, and CPU time is attributed from worker-side work. This is intentionally conservative and documented.
- The runtime flag ensures zero default overhead; the code paths are behind fast checks. We intentionally avoid fine-grained per-token kernel probes to keep this safe for shared environments.

Commits:
- 1) init: add hw split metric collectors and basic exporter hooks
- 2) replaybench: synthetic replaybench service + trace consumer
- 3) dashboards: grafana panels + alert rule + docs
- 4) tests/lint: unit tests for metrics + fix lint failures

- services/runtime/metrics/hw_token_metrics.go

- services/replaybench/main.go

Review thread summary: 
- Evan Liu: asked for opt-in runtime flag and confirmation that default path is zero-cost; requested unit tests covering label explosion.
- Priya (author): implemented the flag, added fast-path guard and reduced label cardinality by limiting label values to {cpu,gpu,io} and adding sampling_rate label only when >0.
- Samira Khatri: requested an architectural note on how GPU timestamps are correlated; requested that the dashboard include a baseline historical view and a replay-confirmation toggle.
- Priya: updated the dashboard JSON with a baseline row and added a replaybench badge to panels so operators can mark a spike as replay-confirmed.
- Diego Marquez: asked to gate alert firing on replaybench confirmation for the first rollout to avoid noisy alerts; we settled on a 48-hour delayed auto-enable for the gating.

CI history: initial run failed lint (golangci) due to unused import in hw_token_metrics.go; second run: tests flaked in replaybench E2E due to a missing env var in CI container; fixed and final run: all checks passed (unit, integration-replay smoke, lint).

Performance/benchmarks: microbenchmarks in services/runtime/metrics/hw_token_metrics_test.go show <0.5% median p50 latency regression when hw_split_enabled=false and ~2-3% overhead when enabled at 100% sampling. Replaybench run (sample=0.01) on a 24h production sample took ~12m and produced stable per-model cost splits.

Operational notes:
- This is behind a runtime flag; rollout plan is: enable for internal tenants on Canary tomorrow, monitor token_hardware_fraction and replaybench confirmations for 72h, then enable opt-in in self-serve for customers.
- Alert SRE-HW-SPLIT-01 will be initially configured as advisory (pager=off) for two weeks.
